nodes.label: BaseRNG
nodes.rationale: An abstract base class enforces a uniform generator interface so callers do not depend on the underlying randomness mechanism.

nodes.label: GlobalRNG
nodes.rationale: A singleton supplies one unpredictable randomness source and avoids accidental duplication or state resets.

nodes.rationale: Bias and Markov-style correlation model detector imbalance, electronic memory, and thermal noise in imperfect QRNG hardware.

nodes.label: RNG Dependency Injection
nodes.rationale: Passing RNG objects into cryptographic helpers permits deterministic and unpredictable sources to be swapped without changing those helpers.

nodes.label: Reproducibility Versus Chaos
nodes.rationale: Tests require repeatable streams while live cryptographic simulations require operating-system entropy.

nodes.label: Layer-Local Agent Placement
nodes.rationale: Each agent remains inside its own architectural layer to prevent cross-layer dependencies.

nodes.label: Simple Rule-Based Agent Design
nodes.rationale: Simple Python decision loops are more reproducible, testable, and academically transparent than an LLM-agent framework for these roles.
nodes.source_location: ## Build Your Own vs. Use an Existing Framework?

nodes.label: Sequential Condition-Dependent QKD Control
nodes.rationale: QKD post-processing already observes state and makes conditional decisions, so formalizing it as agent behavior is academically defensible.

nodes.label: Layered Dependency Direction
nodes.rationale: Upper layers may use lower layers, while lower layers never import upper layers.

nodes.label: Logical Qubit Noise Versus Optical Loss
nodes.norm_label: logical qubit noise versus optical loss
nodes.rationale: CPTP transformations within the logical-qubit space are physically distinct from vacuum or no-detection outcomes caused by photon loss.

nodes.label: Lowercase Package Names
nodes.rationale: Lowercase package names preserve identical import behavior across Windows, Linux, and CI.

nodes.label: Config-and-Seed Reproducibility
nodes.rationale: Every random component receives an injected RNG and experiments should be reproducible from configuration plus seed.

nodes.label: Scientific Clarity
nodes.rationale: Physics checks and cryptographic assumptions should remain explicit, testable, and documented.

nodes.label: Separation of Concerns
nodes.rationale: Randomness, configuration, quantum mathematics, protocol logic, authentication, and experiments belong in distinct modules.

nodes.label: Tests Mirror the Source Tree
nodes.rationale: Mirrored test modules make each architectural layer's behavior and invariants independently verifiable.

nodes.label: Measurement Performance Optimization Strategy
nodes.rationale: Optimization should first remove repeated constant validation and unnecessary collapse work, then use benchmarks before batching or JIT approaches.

nodes.label: Optional Density-State Validation
nodes.rationale: Spectral validation remains safe by default but may be disabled in large experiments after state-producing paths have physics-preservation tests.

nodes.label: POVM Extensibility Boundary
nodes.rationale: APIs remain explicitly projective until B92 introduces a genuinely different measurement model, avoiding a premature generic hierarchy.

nodes.label: Probability Validation Before Clipping
nodes.rationale: Validating ranges before numerical cleanup prevents clipping from hiding physically invalid probability vectors.
